title: Tail-latency weighted SLI taxonomy and protected failover-slice policy
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: Current SLI definitions emphasize p50/p95 averages and per-route availability but fail to capture tail-latency impact on interactive product features. During regional congestion events we observe prioritized routes degrading silently and regional failover floods downstream clusters, causing cascading evictions. Goals: 1) define a tail-latency weighted SLI taxonomy that reserves weight for p99+/tail events, with per-endpoint and per-model variants; 2) design a "protected failover slices" policy (small reserved capacity slices and eviction exemptions) to guarantee minimal throughput for critical routes/customers during cross-region failover; 3) tie circuit-breaker thresholds and load-shedding priorities to a unified error-budget/burn-rate model that respects protected slices.
background: Existing documents define SLOs and tiered error budgets, but lack a concrete mechanism to protect critical tail requests during regional failover. Customer incidents in Q4 2025 showed that naive regional failover increases aggregate tail latency and causes high-priority routes to be evicted under load. This ticket pilots a hybrid approach: quantile-aware SLI weighting + small reserved failover slices (per-tenant or per-route) + burn-rate-aware circuit breakers.
acceptance_criteria: SLI spec produced: includes p50/p95/p99/p999 buckets, and a weighted composite score that can be computed from telemetry
Policy doc for protected failover slices with explicit rules for slice sizing, eviction-exempt criteria, and billing/monitoring hooks
Circuit-breaker tuning guidelines that consume error-budget burn-rate signals and respect protected slice reservations
End-to-end simulation demonstrating >50% reduction in high-priority request evictions during a 30% regional capacity loss scenario
Implementation plan and one experimental rollout to a non-critical region with metrics dashboard and alerting
work_items: Design SLI weighting formula and provide example calculations for text-generation and chat endpoints
Define schema changes for telemetry to emit quantile buckets and weight tags
Prototype protected-slice admission controller in serving runtime (PoC branch)
Instrument circuit-breaker component to read burn-rate signals and protected-slice occupancy
Run chaos simulation (regional network partition + 30% capacity) and capture eviction/latency graphs
Draft runbook updates and console UI mockups to surface protected-slice utilization and remaining error budget

2026-03-04 - Marcus Li: Collected telemetry sample. p99 spikes account for 18% of perceived product errors on low-latency routes. Will prepare quantile histograms.
2026-03-07 - Diego Martinez (review): Suggest we parameterize slice sizing by route criticality and per-tenant SLA tier. Also call out cost accounting implications.
2026-03-09 - Marcus Li: PoC branch created: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/5123. Admission controller implemented as a soft-reservation—starts as local-only experiment.
2026-03-10 - QA: Early simulation shows protected slices reduce high-priority evictions by ~42% but increases average latency on non-protected traffic; need to validate acceptable trade-off.
2026-03-12 - Product (Leah Koh): Product approves pilot for non-critical EU region, but requests a feature flag and dashboard visibility before rollout.
2026-03-13 - Security (Jamal Price): Reviewed; no new data-plane controls required. Recommend audit log entries for slice allocations.
notes: Trade-offs: protecting tail requests improves perceived reliability for premium customers but shifts headroom pressure to other traffic classes. We'll monitor cost and adjust slice sizing dynamically based on observed burn-rate and forecasted load.
